strings.organizationPolicy: An administrator can lock settings with a policy file or a Windows policy key. Locked settings show a lock and the words Set by your organization. An invalid policy is ignored and does not change your settings. Choose a profile on first run or in Settings. A profile locked by your organization cannot be changed.

strings.helpLimits: It checks emails, phones, identity numbers, cards, IBANs, and keys. It does not detect names without a term you add, and it does not detect street addresses. A PDF with no text layer is not read unless image scan is available.
strings.helpLinksBody: This spots link tricks. It does not know every new phishing site. It warns about a lookalike name, a brand on someone else's site, text before @, a dangerous link, a numeric address, and a risky download. In an email or a document it also warns when the words and the link disagree, or when the sender name does not match the address. It does not catch a new phishing site with an ordinary name, a link you click without copying, a QR code, or an attachment that is itself malicious. It is not an antivirus, an email filter, or a browser extension. The public-suffix list used for the site name is dated 2026-10-01.
strings.helpCheckBody: Drop files or a folder on Check, or choose a file. You can also right-click a folder in Explorer after you add the Explorer menu. Review anything that looks sensitive, then make a protected copy. The original file is never changed.
strings.helpClipboardBody: Every copy is checked, including a screenshot and HTML or RTF copied from a page. A picture is read with Windows OCR on this PC. Redact puts sanitized text and HTML back, or a picture with black bars. A picture above the size limit is not checked. The warning appears when a target app is in front, including after you switch to it. You can ignore it once, stop, redact, mark a finding not sensitive, or ignore one selected value in the future. PeritumAI Protect never changes the clipboard without your choice.
strings.helpTermsBody: Settings can add exact names, identifiers, or regular expressions. These rules remain on this PC. Settings can export rules and My terms to a JSON file, or import one. The file is checked before it is stored. Nothing in the file is run. A duplicate id is reported and is not merged.
strings.helpTrayBody: Closing this window keeps protection running in the notification area. Use the tray icon to open, pause, resume, or quit.
strings.helpCaution: PeritumAI Protect uses deterministic rules and does not catch everything. Check the findings before sharing important material.
strings.restoreIntro: Paste an answer that contains tokens such as [[EMAIL_1]], or drop a .txt, .md, or .docx file. Saving writes a new document from the AI's answer. The original layout is not kept. Nothing is sent anywhere.

pii.email.tip: Use a reversible copy if you still need to refer to them, and send the real address only to someone who should have it.

pii.ipv4.text: An IP address can show which network a computer was using.
pii.ipv4.tip: Leave this check off unless you are reading logs. It does not prove who the person is.

pii.dob.text: A date of birth is used to identify people and to answer security questions.
pii.dob.tip: Share the year only when the full date is not needed.

pii.health_id.text: A health-record number can point to someone's medical file.
pii.health_id.tip: Keep the real number in the clinic system. A reversible token is enough in a draft.

pii.matter.text: A number after a case or file label can connect a document to a client, a patient, or an employee.
pii.matter.tip: Add your own number format if this label does not match how you number files.

ref.labels.text: The identifier after this label can point to a person or a matter.
ref.labels.tip: The check covers only that identifier, not the words around it.

ref.finance.text: An invoice or policy number can identify a customer or a contract.
ref.finance.tip: Share it only with the person who already handles that account.

court.us.federal.text: A US federal case number identifies a lawsuit and the people in it.
court.us.federal.tip: Confirm you are allowed to share the number before you paste it.

court.eu.cjeu.text: A Court of Justice or General Court number identifies a case.
court.eu.cjeu.tip: Confirm you are allowed to share the number before you paste it.

fin.card.text: A full card number can be used to charge the card.
fin.card.tip: Do not paste the full number. The result shows only a masked hint.

fin.iban.text: An IBAN can be used to send or request a payment.
fin.iban.tip: Share it only with the person who should be paid.

fin.salary.text: A salary figure shows what someone is paid.
fin.salary.tip: Remove it from a file you share, or use a reversible token in a draft.

secret.aws_access_key.text: Anyone who sees this AWS key can use the account as you, and the bill can land on you.
secret.aws_access_key.tip: Revoke it in AWS if it was already sent, and create a new key.

secret.aws_secret.text: This is the secret half of an AWS key. Together with the access key, it opens the account.
secret.aws_secret.tip: Revoke the key pair if this line was shared.

secret.aws_temp.text: This is a temporary AWS key. It can still use the account until it expires.
secret.aws_temp.tip: Revoke the session if the line was shared, and do not paste it again.

secret.github_pat.text: Anyone who sees this GitHub token can act as you on the repositories it can reach.
secret.github_pat.tip: Revoke the token on GitHub if it was already sent, and create a new one.

secret.gitlab.text: Anyone who sees this GitLab token can act as you on the projects it can reach.
secret.gitlab.tip: Revoke the token if it was already sent, and create a new one.

secret.stripe.text: Anyone who sees this Stripe key can move money or read customers on that account.
secret.stripe.tip: Roll the key in Stripe if it was already sent.

secret.slack.text: Anyone who sees this Slack token can read or post as the app that owns it.
secret.slack.tip: Revoke the token in Slack if it was already sent.

secret.openai_sk.text: Anyone who sees this key can use the service as you, and pay with your account.
secret.openai_sk.tip: Revoke it if it was already sent, and create a new key.

secret.anthropic.text: Anyone who sees this key can use the service as you, and pay with your account.
secret.anthropic.tip: Revoke it if it was already sent, and create a new key.

secret.google_api.text: Anyone who sees this Google API key can call the APIs it is allowed to use, often at your cost.
secret.google_api.tip: Restrict or delete the key in the Google console if it was shared.

secret.jwt.text: This token can carry a signed-in session. Anyone who has it can act as that user until it expires.
secret.jwt.tip: Sign out of that session if the token was pasted, and sign in again.

secret.pem.text: This is a private key. Anyone who has it can pretend to be the server or the person it belongs to.
secret.pem.tip: If it left this PC, treat it as stolen and issue a new key.

secret.entropy.text: This looks like a random secret, such as a password or a key, but the check is not sure.
secret.entropy.tip: Read the line yourself, revoke it if it is a secret, and mark it not sensitive if it is ordinary text.

secret.huggingface.text: Anyone who sees this token can use the Hugging Face account it belongs to.
secret.huggingface.tip: Revoke the token if it was already sent.

secret.sendgrid.text: Anyone who sees this key can send mail through that SendGrid account.
secret.sendgrid.tip: Revoke the key if it was already sent.

secret.npm.text: Anyone who sees this token can publish packages as you on npm.
secret.npm.tip: Revoke the token if it was already sent, and create a new one.

secret.twilio.text: Anyone who sees this Twilio secret can send messages or calls on that account, and you pay.
secret.twilio.tip: Roll the secret in Twilio if it was shared.

secret.azure.text: Anyone who sees this Azure secret can use the app registration it belongs to.
secret.azure.tip: Remove the secret in Azure and create a new one if it was shared.

secret.connection.text: This looks like a connection string or a web address with a password or a key in it.
secret.connection.tip: Change that password if the line was shared, and keep the new one out of the chat.

secret.password_assignment.text: This line looks like a password written next to a label.
secret.password_assignment.tip: Do not paste passwords into a chat. Store them in a password manager.

secret.discord.text: Anyone who sees this Discord token can control the bot or the account it belongs to.
secret.discord.tip: Reset the token in Discord if it was shared.

clickfix.command.text: A website put a command on your clipboard. Real sites never ask you to paste commands into Run or a terminal.
clickfix.command.tip: Do not run it. Clear the clipboard.

crypto.swap.text: Your copied wallet address was replaced by another one. This is a sign of clipboard malware.
crypto.swap.tip: Do not send the funds. Copy the address again from the source you trust, and check this PC for malware.

hidden.content.text: This text is hidden in the document or the clipboard. A person can miss it, and a chat can still read it.
hidden.content.tip: Use Clean for sharing, or make a protected copy, so the hidden text is left out.

hidden.instruction.text: This text tells an AI to ignore earlier instructions or to hide something from you.
hidden.instruction.tip: Do not paste it into a chat. If you did not write it, treat the file as untrusted.

hidden.invisible-unicode.text: Invisible characters can hide words between the letters you see.
hidden.invisible-unicode.tip: Clean for sharing removes them. Read the preview before you send the file.

hidden.unicode-tags.text: Unicode tag characters can spell a hidden message that does not show on screen.
hidden.unicode-tags.tip: Do not trust the file until those characters are removed.

hidden.mixed-scripts.text: Letters from two alphabets in one word can make a fake name or a fake address look real.
hidden.mixed-scripts.tip: Retype the word yourself if you meant to send it.

hidden.html-comment.text: An HTML comment is hidden on the page, but a chat can still read it.
hidden.html-comment.tip: Clean for sharing drops comments. Do not rely on a comment staying private.

hidden.html.text: This text is in the HTML but it is not shown, for example in a script, a hidden style, or a hidden element.
hidden.html.tip: A protected copy keeps the visible words and drops the hidden ones.

hidden.offscreen.text: This text is placed off the visible page, so you do not see it while a chat still can.
hidden.offscreen.tip: Clean for sharing leaves it out.

hidden.alt.text: Alt text and title text are for accessibility and tooltips. They can also hide a message.
hidden.alt.tip: Read the alt text before you send the page. Remove it if you did not write it.

hidden.office-text.text: A marked-hidden run in the document is not shown in the usual view, but it is still in the file.
hidden.office-text.tip: Clean for sharing removes hidden text. The original file is not changed.

hidden.office-sheet.text: A hidden sheet, row, column, or slide can hold data you do not see while scrolling.
hidden.office-sheet.tip: Clean for sharing deletes a hidden sheet. Check the list of what was removed.

hidden.white-text.text: White or near-white text on a light background is easy to miss and still in the file.
hidden.white-text.tip: Clean for sharing leaves it out of the copy.

hidden.pdf-invisible.text: This PDF text is set not to be drawn, so you do not see it on the page.
hidden.pdf-invisible.tip: The clean copy is text from the visible page only. Layout is not kept.

hidden.pdf-tiny.text: Text under 2 points is too small to read on the page and can still be copied out.
hidden.pdf-tiny.tip: The clean copy leaves it out.

hidden.pdf-white.text: White or near-white text can sit on the page without being noticed.
hidden.pdf-white.tip: The clean copy leaves it out.

hidden.pdf-outside.text: This text sits outside the page box, so it does not show when you read the page.
hidden.pdf-outside.tip: The clean copy leaves it out.

hidden.pdf-optional.text: This text is on a hidden optional-content layer in the PDF.
hidden.pdf-optional.tip: The clean copy uses the visible page text and leaves that layer out.

hidden.pdf-annotation.text: A PDF note or comment can hold text that is not part of the page you are reading.
hidden.pdf-annotation.tip: Read the comments before you share the file. The clean copy leaves them out.

hidden.pdf-form.text: A form field can hold a value that is easy to overlook on the page.
hidden.pdf-form.tip: Check the field values before you share the PDF.

hidden.pdf-info.text: Document info and XMP can hold names, titles, and paths that are not on the page.
hidden.pdf-info.tip: Clean for sharing drops that info. It does not change the original file.

unchecked.password.text: The file is locked with a password, so it was not read. That is not a clean result.
unchecked.password.tip: Unlock a copy yourself and check that copy. This app does not remove the password.

unchecked.unreadable.text: The file could not be read, so nothing in it was checked. That is not a clean result.
unchecked.unreadable.tip: Ask for another copy. Do not send this one as if it were clean.

unchecked.legacy.text: This version cannot read this older file type. That is not a clean result.
unchecked.legacy.tip: Save a docx, xlsx, pptx, or txt copy and check that file.

unchecked.encrypted.text: An entry in the archive is encrypted, so it was left out. That entry was not checked.
unchecked.encrypted.tip: The rest of the archive can still be checked. The encrypted entry is not a clean result.

unchecked.image-size.text: The picture is too large to read here, so it was not checked. That is not a clean result.
unchecked.image-size.tip: Make a smaller copy and check that copy. The large picture was not called clean.

unchecked.ocr.text: Windows OCR is not available on this PC, so the picture was not read.
unchecked.ocr.tip: Add an OCR language in Windows Settings, then check the picture again.

incomplete.size.text: The file expands past 256 MB, so the check stopped. The rest was not read.
incomplete.size.tip: Do not treat the file as clean, and do not expect a protected copy.

incomplete.part.text: One part is larger than 64 MB, so the check stopped. That part was not read.
incomplete.part.tip: Do not treat the file as clean, and do not expect a protected copy.

incomplete.parts.text: The package has more than 10,000 parts, so the check stopped.
incomplete.parts.tip: Do not treat the file as clean, and do not expect a protected copy.

incomplete.ratio.text: The file is compressed more than 100 to 1, which can be a zip bomb. The check stopped.
incomplete.ratio.tip: Do not open it elsewhere to force a result, and do not expect a protected copy.

incomplete.nesting.text: Packages are nested more than 3 deep, so the check stopped.
incomplete.nesting.tip: Do not treat the file as clean, and do not expect a protected copy.

incomplete.pdf-pages.text: The PDF has more than 2,000 pages, so the check stopped before the end.
incomplete.pdf-pages.tip: Later pages were not read. Split the PDF and check the parts you need.

incomplete.pdf-time.text: The PDF took too long to read, so the check stopped before the end.
incomplete.pdf-time.tip: What was not read is not a clean result. Try a smaller file.

incomplete.stopped.text: The check stopped before the end. What was not read is not a clean result.
incomplete.stopped.tip: Do not send the file as if it were fully checked.

incomplete.entropy.text: The high-entropy check was skipped for part of this file. The other checks still ran.
incomplete.entropy.tip: A long random-looking secret in the skipped part may not be listed.

link.text_mismatch.text: The words you see name one site, and the link goes to another.
link.text_mismatch.tip: Look at the address before you open it. Do not trust the visible words alone.

link.lookalike.text: The address is a lookalike of a known name.
link.lookalike.tip: Type the site yourself instead of using this link.

link.brand_elsewhere.text: A known brand appears in the address, but the site belongs to someone else.
link.brand_elsewhere.tip: The brand word is not the site you will open.

link.sender_mismatch.text: The sender name names a brand, and the sending address is on a different site.
link.sender_mismatch.tip: Check the address in From, not only the display name.

link.reply_to_differs.text: Reply goes to a different address than the one that sent the message.
link.reply_to_differs.tip: A reply may not go back to the sender you see.

link.userinfo_trick.text: The part before @ is ignored. The link goes to the site after it.
link.userinfo_trick.tip: Read the site after @ before you open the link.

link.dangerous_scheme.text: This link can run a command or open a file instead of a web page.

link.ip_host.text: The link uses a numeric address instead of a site name.
link.ip_host.tip: A number is easy to disguise. Prefer a name you already know.

link.risky_download.text: The link points at a file that can run on this PC.
link.risky_download.tip: Download it only from a site you already trust.

link.shortener.text: A short link hides where it goes.
link.shortener.tip: Open it only when you already know the site.

link.odd_port.text: This link uses an unusual port.
link.odd_port.tip: Check the address before you open it.
